$comment: What a discovery answer becomes, on both hosts: the servers the plugin is handed, with no credential field, and the hosts each server's credential is bound to. `typed` is what the viewer typed into the plugin's url fields; only an IP literal a connection's address and port match binds, over the scheme typed, and confirmed by the server's identity before first use. A case names a service in contracts/link-logins.json, or one of declarations.json's. test/link-login.test.js walks it through src/host/link-sign-in.js and LinkBindingRecordTest through LinkSignIn.kt.

cases.why: a shared server is handed over without its token and bound on each https connection the reach admits and on the address the viewer typed; an owned server, a player, a server whose token is the account's, one that cannot be read, one over http and one with no token are not bound, and the unreadable one is left out
cases.about: NOT A RECORDING: the shape of https://clients.plex.tv/api/v2/resources written from Plex's documentation, since no account exists to record one; addresses are from the documentation ranges

cases.why: a reach that does not admit the connections binds only the typed address
a typed address on another port matches no connection
a typed name is never matched by what it resolves to
a typed https address is bound over https
an answer that is not a list is no answer

expect.refused: the account answered no list of servers

cases.why: nor is one that is not JSON

expect.refused: the account answered no list of servers

cases.why: an empty list is an account with no servers
a server whose token is not one a host keeps is left out
a service that declares no owner owns nothing, whatever an entry's fields say, so every server is bound but one whose token is the account's
